beats.say: On a phone the address bar is short, and most of the address is hidden. Scammers count on that.
Look at this address: the official name comes first, but the real owner of the site is the part at the end.
There are other tricks too: letters swap places, a word is added, a similar digit replaces a letter.
On a suspicious address type nothing, close the page and tell technical support.

scenes.prompt: Match each fake address with the official one it imitates.
scenes.explain: The difference is small: the official name placed in front, a digit, two swapped letters or an extra word. Always read the address from the end.

scenes.prompt: Put the steps for checking an address on a phone in order.

items.label: Tap the address bar to see the full address
Find the last part of the domain
Compare it letter by letter with the official address
If anything differs, close it without typing

scenes.explain: On a phone the end of the address is often hidden, so open it fully first. If the official name is not at the end, the site is fake.

points: On a phone, open the full address and read it from the end
Even if the official name comes first, the real owner is the part at the end
If you typed a password, change it on the official site and report it
